description.summary: windows that are known again, where they were

protocol.description:
Dukovo's window server keeps where a window was: on which screen, where on it and how large, and whether it was maximized or snapped to a zone. A window that shows again shows there. To know a window again, the window server needs a name for it that lasts longer than the window does, and only the window's program has one: the main window, the terminal of one profile, the document of one path.
With this protocol a program gives a window such a name. A program that names none of its windows has them placed as new windows are.

interface.name: dukovo_session_manager_v1

description.summary: names windows for the window server to know again

interface.description: The global a program binds to name its windows.

entry.name: bad_name
entry.summary: the name is empty, longer than 255 bytes, or not UTF-8

request.name: destroy
request.description: The names given with the manager stay.

request.name: name_window

description.summary: give a toplevel a name that lasts

request.description:
Gives a toplevel a name the program will give the same window again when it next makes it. The name is the program's own and means nothing to the window server, which knows a window by its toplevel's application id and this name together. A name of no bytes, of more than 255, or that is not UTF-8 text, is the bad_name error.
A toplevel that is named before the first commit of its surface, and was known by the same application id and name before, is asked in its first configure event to be drawn at the size it had, maximized or tiled as it was, and shows where it was: on the screen it was on if that screen is there. The program draws it as any configure event asks. A toplevel that was not known is placed as a new window is.
From then on the window server keeps where the window is, for the next time. A toplevel named after it first showed stays where it is and is kept from then on.
A name is one window's at a time: while a toplevel of the same application id has it, another that is given it has no name. A toplevel whose application id is not set has no name either. Naming a toplevel again gives it the new name in place of the old.
